summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, having also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.
Mery Cecconi is an Indologist. She is a PhD candidate at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the doctoral supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram (born 1956) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer, later serving at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris (1946–1999) was a scholar in Tibetology and history. He studied at Durham University and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove, later holding positions at Oxford and Harvard, and founding the International Association for Tibetan Studies.
Michael Balk worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Royal Library of Berlin (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute, UC Berkeley, and Cornell University.

Michael Bernays (1834–1897) studied at the Universities of Bonn and Heidelberg under Adolf Holtzmann. He later held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael C. Shapiro (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty at the University of Washington from circa 1970 to 2017, becoming Professor Emeritus of Hindi around 2017.

Michael Carrithers (born 1945) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Wesleyan and Oxford, he taught at the London School of Economics, Oxford, and Durham University, becoming Professor of Anthropology in 1992.

Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong, later serving on the faculty at the University of Sydney (~1989–2005).
Michael J. Conway specializes in Buddhist studies. He serves as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and is affiliated with the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Michael Eido Luetchford (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an engineering degree from the University of Bradford, studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima (~1977–2007), and founded Windbell Publications.
Michael Friedrich (born 1955) is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from the University of Munich. After working at Munich (1983–1986), he was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

Michael G. Morony (born 1939) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA, becoming a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1974.

Michael Hahn (1941–2014) was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He held major posts at the University of Bonn and the University of Marburg.
Michael Harack specializes in religious studies and Sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).
Michael Hookham is a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa beginning in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt (born 1957) is an Indologist and linguist who completed his BA and doctorate at the University of London. He spent his career at SOAS University of London, serving as Department Head and Associate Dean.

Michael I. Como is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Sinology who studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He serves as Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University.
